classification_semantics.supported: The licensed surface already meets the provider contract without semantic repair.
classification_semantics.adaptable: A real licensed primitive exists and can retain its semantics behind the provider mapping. Production admission may still require licensed-surface augmentation for safety evidence the primitive cannot currently expose; ncm_change_required records that distinction.
classification_semantics.blocking: A related primitive exists, but using it for this capability would violate a mandatory semantic guarantee until the licensed implementation or topology changes.
classification_semantics.unsupported: No callable primitive implements the capability; it must not be declared.

formats: .bdbm: BDBMZIP01 plus ZIP containing vectors.pt and metadata.json
BDBMENC01: legacy machine-fingerprint encrypted container accepted for compatibility
raw ZIP without magic: accepted with a warning
compatibility: new .bdbm output is portable between machines
legacy encrypted .bdbm requires the originating machine fingerprint
legacy .pt load rewrites its version marker to 1.0 and attempts a best-effort pre-migration backup
.bdbm load does not run migrate_state or reject an incompatible state version

observed_outcomes.outcome: missing state file leaves initialized empty memory
unknown/corrupt container raises in BDBMContainer.load but TextMemory._load_impl catches and logs it, leaving initialized state
missing sections in a decoded state are applied selectively rather than rejected as an incompatible whole
store_record mutates RAM before save; save failure returns an error without describing whether the provider effect remains in memory
shutdown save failure is logged and shutdown continues

persistence.load_failure_policy: fail_closed is required; the observed log-and-continue behavior is nonconformant and blocks readiness
persistence.crash_safety: blocking: Path.write_bytes replaces the final state directly with no temporary sibling, atomic rename, file fsync, or directory fsync
persistence.scope_isolation: blocking: one process resolves one shared state file; no exact TraceDecay scope is represented in the file or health surface
persistence.privacy_note: portable metadata.json contains key/value text, stable IDs, and provenance inside an unencrypted ZIP; provider admission must enforce the TraceDecay privacy contract before use

lifecycle.startup: TextMemory construction attempts auto-load; the server forces lazy embedder model access before marking its server task running
lifecycle.readiness: HTTP health returns ready when status returns success, independently of a verified load result or state/config/build/scope identity
lifecycle.shutdown: WebSocket connections and HTTP listener are stopped, then memory.save is attempted; failure is logged
lifecycle.topology: one BDBMServer owns one TextMemory, one CommandHandler, one session cache, WebSocket transport, and HTTP fallback
lifecycle.recovery: backup/restore primitives exist, but restore catches load failure internally and can return success after no compatible state was applied

threading_observations.outcome: the actual HTTP transport overlapped bounded synthetic handler coroutines at probe levels 1, 2, 4, and 8; this establishes transport overlap only, not model, persistence, CPU, or internal provider parallelism
production HTTP requests are submitted from HTTP worker threads to one daemon asyncio loop
store_record/search/list and several maintenance commands serialize through one CommandHandler asyncio lock
TextMemory public mutation/read methods generally use a process-local RLock

update_center/delete_center dispatch direct center access with asyncio.to_thread outside CommandHandler.lock and TextMemory._lock; update targets absent singular text attributes, while delete changes active/intensity without clearing the actual plural text arrays

cancellation_observations.outcome: the client timed out; the bounded synthetic handler later took its normal-return branch and no CancelledError was observed; this proves non-cancellation only for this synthetic transport request, not real TextMemory/model/persistence work or mutation-effect certainty
HTTPFallbackServer._submit_command waits on run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result() and has no socket-disconnect path to future.cancel or a provider cancellation signal
LocalDaemonClient maps its own HTTP timeout to DEADLINE_EXCEEDED but transmits neither an absolute deadline nor a live cancellation token
the 2 second connect and 30 second read budgets apply independently to the health preflight and command request, not to one end-to-end provider operation
there is no server operation identity or effect query with which to reconcile a timed-out mutation

errors: CommandHandler returns stable string codes for validation and known command failures, while unexpected exceptions collapse to INTERNAL_ERROR
HTTP command-level errors normally retain HTTP 200 and a JSON status=error envelope
LocalDaemonClient exposes only a small safe code set; SAVE_FAILED, WRITE_ERROR, DUPLICATE_MEMORY_ID, and INVALID_PARAMS are collapsed to INTERNAL_ERROR
no mutation response reports committed none/applied/partial/unknown state, provider generation, or a queryable operation identity
inspectability: status exposes security state, active session count, and best-effort memory stats
search exposes bounded stable-ID semantic results without center indices
list_memories exposes stable-ID pages but first materializes up to 1,000,000 records and has no byte budget or generation-bound cursor
graph exposes up to 250 selected nodes with explicit truncation
there is no delivery-outcome, source-influence, state-generation, recovery, snapshot-metadata, or capability-status inspection view

measurements.expectation: Every Python source file compiles without writing bytecode.
Required probe entrypoints are inventoried without treating presence as support.
HTTP health must distinguish product liveness from loaded-state readiness and expose build/config/state identity before claiming ready.
Measure transport-level concurrency without inferring that the real model or persistence layer executes concurrently.
A client timeout must not be reported as server-side cancellation; completion after disconnect remains an unknown-effect risk for mutations.
Health/load evidence exposes actual loaded-state, build, config, schema, and generation identity.
An identical observation retry is measured for effect count and reinforcement, not assumed idempotent.
Side-effect-free search returns no more than the explicit result bound with stable IDs and provenance.
Actual TextMemory reads and writes are measured at 1, 2, 4, and 8 concurrent callers.
Client timeout/cancel outcome is separated from server completion and committed-effect certainty.
Two explicit isolated state paths do not expose each other's admitted memory IDs.
A save/restart cycle preserves the admitted memory identity and bounded recall product.
Interrupted publication and incompatible restore fail explicitly without silent reset or false success.
